caption: The drawing is a technical illustration of a mahogany tea table from Philadelphia, dating to the third quarter of the eighteenth century, rendered on a beige or light tan background with black ink lines and text. The composition consists of three main views of the table: in the top left, there is a rectangular plan labeled “PLAN of TOP” and “PLAN of BASE,” showing the tabletop’s dimensions (34 inches by 22 inches), rounded corners, decorative bevel, and bead details; the drawing provides measurements and indicates a 5/8” bevel and 1/4” bead. Below this plan view, a “FRONT ELEVATION” shows the table’s front side, emphasizing its overall length (34 inches), height (27 3/8 inches), and the ornate, curved cabriole legs with carved details at the knees and ball-and-claw feet. To the right, a “SIDE ELEVATION” presents the table from the side, showing its depth (22 inches) and repeating the details of the leg design and apron. The parts of the table are neatly divided by dotted lines indicating symmetry, and at the upper right, the title block gives the description: '"TEA TABLE MAHOGANY" PHILADELPHIA, THIRD QUARTER OF XVIII CENTURY.' All lines and notations are in black, consistent throughout the drawing, and the style is precise and architectural.
title: Tea Table
